title: The Honest Room
subtitle: Ten weeks to say the sentence you've been carrying, and stop performing the woman who never has to.

week_list.title: The Room
week_list.opening_line: Eleven women are going to look at you for two hours and not one of them is going to try to help you.
week_list.stakes: Skip this and you spend ten weeks in a room you are still auditioning for, saying the second-truest thing every single time.
week_list.pull_quote: Advice is how a room gets away from a woman. It looks like care and it is an exit.

blocks.v: The four rules of the room

blocks.title: What holds the room together
rows: No advice
Advice is how a room avoids a woman without anybody noticing.
No rescuing
The silence is where she says the second half of it.
No joke on the end
The joke takes it back and a polite room lets you.
It stays here
You cannot be honest in a room that leaks.

blocks.text: Putting away falsehood, let each of you speak the truth with his neighbor, for we are members one of another.
blocks.why: The reason given is not integrity. It is membership.

blocks.title: The inner work — The Rooms You Perform In

items.head: Name your last three rooms
items.sub: Any three rooms you performed in this week — kitchen, office, group chat.

items.head: Who was in each one
items.sub: And which version of you walked in.

items.head: Circle the widest gap
items.sub: Between the version that walked in and the true one.

items.head: Write one sentence
items.sub: What should have been said in that room instead.

items.head: Say it aloud alone
items.sub: In the room where it belonged, or the closest room you have.

items.head: Bring it to session unimproved
items.sub: Not the polished version. The one you actually wrote.

blocks.title: Done means
items: The four rules read aloud once
The six-step inner work done in one sitting
One plain sentence said in session, under twelve words
Seven daily logs
One hedging incident named by name
blocks.demo: Say the sentence in under twelve words, no preamble, no joke on the end, eyes up.

week_list.title: The Inventory
week_list.opening_line: You have a story about every one of your patterns, and the story is the thing keeping it alive.
week_list.stakes: Skip the flat inventory and you keep mistaking the story for the fix — insight without a flat line changes nothing.
week_list.pull_quote: Insight is the reason you can name it. It is also, precisely, the reason you have not stopped.

blocks.v: The story, and the flat line

blocks.title: Cut every pattern down to one sentence
rows: Over-explaining
I keep talking after the answer is finished.
The pre-emptive apology
I say sorry before I ask for anything.
The disappearing act
I stop answering people for four days at a time.
Managing the room
I watch faces and adjust until nobody is uncomfortable.
The tap-out
I make a joke the second somebody gets close.

blocks.text: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man who looks intently at his natural face in a mirror. For he looks at himself and goes away and at once forgets what he was like.
blocks.why: Naming a pattern in the mirror and being changed by it are two different acts.

items.sub: Every known pattern you have. Do not think, list.

items.head: One line each
items.sub: No "because." Say it and stop.

items.head: Count them
items.sub: Write the number at the top of the page.

items.head: Circle the one someone else pays for

items.head: Read the whole list aloud, standing
items.sub: Flat, no explanation, start to finish.

week_list.title: The Pause
week_list.opening_line: You have never once let a correction land — you have been answering them before they finished arriving.
week_list.stakes: Skip the pause and every correction you're ever offered keeps costing the giver more than it costs you, until nobody offers you one again.
week_list.pull_quote: A correction is cheap for you and expensive for the woman giving it. You have had that backwards your whole adult life.

blocks.v: The three seconds

blocks.title: What you've been doing, and what you do this week
rows: She finishes the sentence, you start talking on her last word

Say thank you and take it home.
She's right and you agree loudly and perform the change

Let the silence run out.

blocks.cue: Three seconds of silence before you answer. Count them.

blocks.text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend.
blocks.why: A wound that comes from someone who stayed is not the same thing as an injury.

week_list.title: The Performance
week_list.opening_line: The woman you perform is built for an audience that left years ago, and most of them would not recognize the act as being about them.
week_list.stakes: Keep running the performance and you'll spend the rest of your life auditioning for people who are no longer watching.
week_list.pull_quote: Not laying down a pattern. Laying down an audience.

blocks.v: The performances, and their tells

blocks.title: Five performances and the body's tell
rows: The competent one
Plan offered unasked. Voice drops and speeds up at once.
The easy one
Joke on the last word of the hard thing. Face moves before mouth does.
The grateful one
Reframes into a lesson while still bleeding. Chin lifts, shoulders rise.
The fine one
Says "fine" twice in one answer. Hands go flat and still.
The deep one
Insight delivered fluently in the room's vocabulary. Eyes go to middle distance and stay.

blocks.text: For am I now seeking the approval of man, or of God? Or am I trying to please man? If I were still trying to please man, I would not be a servant of Christ.

week_list.title: The Sentence
week_list.opening_line: There is one sentence you have never said out loud to anybody, and you knew which one it was before you finished reading this line.
week_list.stakes: Carry it one more year and it keeps costing you exactly what it's cost you every year so far — this is the week that ends.
week_list.pull_quote: It is almost never a confession. It is usually small, usually old, and its whole power is that it has never once been outside your body.

blocks.v: What the sentence usually is

blocks.title: Five properties, and why they matter
rows: Short — under twelve words
If it is long, you are still building the case for it.
Not a confession
More often something you want, or something you believe about yourself.
No "because"
Say it and stop.
Costly to write
Chest tightens while your hand is still moving. The only reliable test.
Old
You have been carrying it years, not weeks.

blocks.text: For when I kept silent, my bones wasted away through my groaning all day long.
But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another.

week_list.title: The Morning After
week_list.opening_line: Eleven women arrive wanting to update the room on last week, and the update is the take-back wearing a nice coat.
week_list.stakes: Skip naming the take-back, and the sentence you finally said last week quietly un-says itself — and you will have said it for nothing.
week_list.pull_quote: You are not going to be punished for it. You are going to have to live with having said it.

blocks.v: The take-back
The take-back is not weakness and not a decision. It is the fastest reflex you own and it is faster than your thinking.

blocks.text: Let what you say be simply 'Yes' or 'No'; anything more than this comes from evil.
blocks.why: The clarifying message you want to send is the "anything more." Taking the words back doesn't un-believe them. It only leaves you holding both.

blocks.text: I believed, even when I spoke: I was greatly afflicted.

blocks.label: The return
blocks.cue: You flinched. Come back and say it again straight, same night.

items.head: One tick, every time

items.head: Three words
items.sub: Where you were standing when you reached for it.

items.head: No clarifying message

week_list.title: The Ask
week_list.opening_line: Every woman here is running a rule she never agreed to out loud, in somebody else's voice, and has been calling it common sense for thirty years.
week_list.stakes: Skip the ask and you keep mistaking a rule you never agreed to for common sense — for another thirty years.
week_list.pull_quote: Ask boldly. Then walk out and prepare like it is coming.

blocks.v: The rule you never agreed to
The lie is not a thought, it is a skill — ten thousand clean reps, no coach needed any more. You do not argue with a drilled thing. You out-rep it.

blocks.text: You do not have, because you do not ask.
Or which one of you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone? ... how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
blocks.why: He does not say you asked badly. He says the request was never made. Children ask for a named thing.

week_list.opening_line: On Monday there is no room, no eleven women, and nothing arranged to hold what she built here.

blocks.v: I stayed in friendships that weren't honest with me. Long after I knew it — the small lies, the things happening behind my back, the loyalty that only worked to my face — I stayed. I called it being loving. It was being slow.

There was a sentence I owed more than one woman I called close, and I never once said it plainly: I know you are not being honest with me, and I am staying anyway. I didn't say those words out loud. What I did instead was smaller and cost more — I made the excuse for her before she asked me to. Every time I answered, I was saying the sentence without saying it.

It cost me years. Not a season — years, plural, of my time and attention going to people who were not fully with me. Every year I spent re-learning that lesson was a year I did not spend on the friendships that were honest the whole time.

For years I was also in a relationship that came with restraints I never said out loud. I couldn't be social, couldn't be part of a community, couldn't just be around people. I told myself it was fine. I never said the sentence: this is not okay, and it is getting worse.

I had a business, and it was doing well. Then the restraints living in my marriage started living in my company, and I watched something I had built start to come apart, and I still didn't say it. The last restraint was the biggest: he wanted me to stop working altogether. So I did. Then, once the business was gone and I was home, he told me he had wanted that on purpose — and that he didn't want to be together anymore. Silence didn't protect any of it. It just delayed the loss and let it grow while I wasn't looking.
Naming it is not stopping it

Being able to name a pattern is not the same as being able to stop it. You can know exactly what you do, say it fluently in a therapist's vocabulary, and still do it again next Tuesday. This room is not for naming. You already know how to name things. This room is for doing the thing you named, in front of people, on a day it costs you something.

blocks.prompt: What has the performance actually gotten you? Be fair to it before you retire it.

blocks.title: Done means
items: Four performances named, with the person and the year for each
One marked still-here or gone, honestly
One performance retired out loud, standing
What you'll do instead, written down
blocks.demo: Stop mid-sentence in front of eleven women, name the performance you're running, and say the true version straight.

blocks.prompt: Who has never met the real woman, and for how long?

blocks.v: There is one sentence you have never said out loud to anybody, and you knew which one it was before you finished reading this line.
It is almost never a confession. It is usually small, usually old, and its whole power is that it has never once been outside your body.

blocks.title: Five properties, and why they matter
rows: Short — under twelve words
If it is long, you are still building the case for it.
Not a confession
More often something you want, or something you believe about yourself.
No "because"
Say it and stop.
Costly to write
Chest tightens while your hand is still moving. The only reliable test.
Old
You have been carrying it years, not weeks.

blocks.text: For when I kept silent, my bones wasted away through my groaning all day long.
But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another.

blocks.title: A note on this week's teaching
blocks.v: A worked example of the sentence itself and of the freeze that can happen right before it's said are still pending from the source material. Rather than invent them, this week runs on the framework and the inner-work steps alone.

blocks.prompt: Write ten candidate sentences — everything you've never said out loud to anybody. Don't rank them yet.

blocks.title: Continue the inner work — The Sentence

items.head: Mark the physical one
items.sub: The one your body reacted to while writing it.

items.head: Cut it to twelve words
items.sub: No more.

items.head: Carry it a day untouched
items.sub: Don't reread it. Don't edit it.

blocks.title: This page is not shared
blocks.v: This week's journal entries are not posted to the Circle. Write it as honestly as you need to.

blocks.prompt: Write the sentence and the year you began carrying it.

items.head: Say it alone, standing
items.sub: Out loud, to an empty room.

items.head: Prepare to say it once in the room
items.sub: Eyes up. Then hold three seconds of silence with no rescue.

blocks.prompt: What did you believe would happen if it were heard? Describe the specific scene you've been avoiding.

blocks.title: Done means
items: Ten candidate sentences written
One marked as physical, cut to twelve words
Said alone, standing, out loud
Said once in the room, eyes up, three seconds held
blocks.demo: Say the sentence in twelve words or fewer, eyes up, and hold three seconds of silence while the room does nothing.

blocks.prompt: Describe the three seconds after you said it — your shoulders, throat, hands. Not the room's reaction. Yours.

blocks.v: Eleven women arrive wanting to update the room on last week, and the update is the take-back wearing a nice coat.
The take-back is not weakness and not a decision. It is the fastest reflex you own and it is faster than your thinking.

blocks.text: Let what you say be simply 'Yes' or 'No'; anything more than this comes from evil.
blocks.why: The clarifying message you want to send is the "anything more." Taking the words back doesn't un-believe them. It only leaves you holding both.

blocks.text: I believed, even when I spoke: I was greatly afflicted.

blocks.label: The return
blocks.cue: You flinched. Come back and say it again straight, same night.

blocks.prompt: Where were you standing each time this week you reached to make last week's sentence smaller? Name the rooms.

items.head: One tick, every time
items.sub: Every time you reach to make the sentence smaller.

items.head: Three words
items.sub: Where you were standing when you reached for it.

items.head: No clarifying message
items.sub: The urge to send "what I meant was" is the take-back. Let it pass.

blocks.prompt: Who is the clarifying message actually for? Write her name and what she would have to think of you.

items.head: Say it again straight
items.sub: Same night if you can. Same voice, no softening.

items.head: Count your log
items.sub: A high number is not failure — it's data.

blocks.prompt: What is different in your house now that the sentence is outside your body?

blocks.title: Done means
items: The take-back log kept all week, honestly, even a high number
No clarifying message sent about last week's sentence
One take-back said straight again, same night
Session walked into without an update on last week
blocks.demo: Walk into session and say nothing about last week — no update, no reference, no joke about it. Answer the first question in your own plain voice.

days.title: The Rule You Never Agreed To

blocks.v: Every woman here is running a rule she never agreed to out loud, in somebody else's voice, and has been calling it common sense for thirty years.
The lie is not a thought, it is a skill — ten thousand clean reps, no coach needed any more. You do not argue with a drilled thing. You out-rep it.

blocks.text: You do not have, because you do not ask.
Or which one of you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone? ... how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
blocks.why: He does not say you asked badly. He says the request was never made. Children ask for a named thing.

blocks.prompt: Write the rule running your life, in quotation marks, in the voice it arrives in. Then write the year you agreed to it.

blocks.title: Continue the inner work — The Ask

items.head: Disagree with the rule, standing
items.sub: Once, out loud.

items.head: Write ten wants, by hand
items.sub: No ranking, no crossing out.

items.head: Cut to one
items.sub: Specific, nameable, dateable.

blocks.prompt: Circle the want you'd be most embarrassed to admit.

items.head: Strip every hedge
items.sub: No "maybe," no "if it's okay."

items.head: Ask it out loud, standing, alone
items.sub: Before the session.

blocks.prompt: Write the ask, what you're afraid the answer is, and what you'll do the next morning either way.

Every hedge stripped from the final ask
The ask said out loud, alone, before session
blocks.demo: Say the ask in the room, standing, one sentence with a named thing, no preamble, no hedge, no joke, hold three seconds.

blocks.v: Eleven women have been watching one woman for two months and every one of them can see the thing she cannot.
Receiving is the verb almost nobody in here has.

blocks.text: What do you have that you did not receive?
blocks.why: Everything you are proud of arrived in somebody's hands.

blocks.text: Iron sharpens iron, and one man sharpens another.
blocks.why: Both pieces of iron lose something. Sharpening is not free for either of them.

blocks.label: Eyes up
blocks.cue: Keep your eyes up while you say the hard thing, and while she says hers.

blocks.prompt: What have you been calling humility, and what year did you start calling it that?

items.sub: Including the unflattering guess you wouldn't repeat. Fold the page.

items.head: Say your ask, standing
items.sub: Stay standing through the whole round.

items.sub: A date or a detail — "you're doing amazing" does not count.

blocks.demo: Take a true good thing said about you in front of eleven women — thank you, eyes up, three seconds — without explaining, correcting, or handing one back to be polite.

blocks.v: Half this room went and had it. Half has a name, a date, and no nerve.
Unspotted is the point. No room, no facilitator, no eleven women — one kitchen, one person, four shapes under full load.

blocks.text: Leave your gift there before the altar and go. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
blocks.why: The instruction interrupts the worship, not the other way round.

blocks.text: If possible, so far as it depends on you, live peaceably with all.
blocks.why: Two limits in one sentence, and both of them are mercy.

blocks.prompt: Retrieve the name from your week-three page. What has she been trying to tell you for a year?

blocks.prompt: What is true tonight that wasn't true this morning?

blocks.v: On Monday there is no room, no eleven women, and nothing arranged to hold what she built here.
Unspotted is not abandonment. It is what a progression is for.

blocks.text: Every place that the sole of your foot will tread upon I have given to you.
Forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus.
blocks.why: Given, past tense, already decided — and still requiring feet.
